title: Your First Case App - Quiz
description: Test your understanding of creating PEGA applications using App Studio

questions.question: What is the first step when creating a new PEGA application?
options: Plan the application structure and requirements
questions.explanation: Planning the application structure and understanding requirements is crucial before starting development to ensure you build the right solution.

questions.question: A case type represents a unit of work that progresses through various stages until completion.
questions.explanation: True. A case type defines the structure and lifecycle of work units, such as service requests, that move through different stages from creation to completion.

questions.question: In a Service Request application, which of these would be an appropriate case stage?
questions.explanation: Request Submission is a logical stage in the case lifecycle where initial request information is collected and validated.

questions.question: You need to collect customer email addresses in your application. What data type should you use?
questions.explanation: Email data type provides built-in validation for email format and ensures data integrity for email addresses.

questions.question: What is the purpose of process flows in PEGA applications?
options: To define how cases move through different stages
questions.explanation: Process flows define the business process and workflow steps that determine how cases progress through different stages and activities.

questions.question: In App Studio, you can create forms using drag-and-drop visual designers.
questions.explanation: True. App Studio provides visual, drag-and-drop form designers that make it easy to create user interfaces without coding.

questions.question: When designing forms, what is a best practice for field organization?
options: Put all fields on one long form
questions.explanation: Grouping related fields together logically improves user experience and makes forms easier to understand and complete.

questions.question: You've created an application but want to test it before deployment. What should you do?
options: Use App Studio's preview feature to test functionality
Ask users to test the live system
Skip testing since it's built with App Studio
questions.explanation: Using App Studio's preview feature allows you to test your application thoroughly before deployment, identifying and fixing issues early.

questions.question: What should you test when validating your application?
options: Both successful workflows and error handling
questions.explanation: Comprehensive testing should include both successful workflows (happy path) and error conditions to ensure the application handles all scenarios properly.

questions.question: After creating your first case application, what would be a logical next step for learning?
options: Learn more about data modeling and advanced UI design
questions.explanation: Learning more about data modeling and advanced UI design builds naturally on the foundation of creating your first application and prepares you for more complex development.

questions.question: Process steps in PEGA should have clear, descriptive names that indicate their purpose.
questions.explanation: True. Clear, descriptive names for process steps improve maintainability and make it easier for team members to understand the application logic.

questions.question: Your Service Request application needs to handle different priority levels. What field type would be most appropriate?
options: Text input where users type priority
questions.explanation: A dropdown with predefined priority options (Low, Medium, High, Urgent) ensures data consistency and makes it easy for users to select the appropriate priority level.
